data.content_ref: inline:The explanation is grounded in a reversed physical premise. If urban emissivity is not systematically lower than rural emissivity — and standard data show asphalt (~0.90–0.98), concrete (~0.92–0.96), and brick (~0.90–0.93) are not lower than, and often exceed, the emissivity of dry natural soils, sands, and rocks typical of arid rural surroundings — then the stated causal chain (lower urban emissivity → slower urban cooling → nocturnal UHI) does not hold. The counterexample is not exotic: it is the very arid-city case the target highlights, where rural dry soil/sand/rock surfaces commonly have emissivities in the same range as urban materials, undermining the claim that emissivity differences drive the gap.
